newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: SOCCER-DAMAGED KNEE MAY END CZECH SKUHRAVY'S CAREER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DAMAGED KNEE MAY END CZECH SKUHRAVY'S CAREER.

text.p: The career of Czech international striker Tomas Skuhravy, who scored 58 goals in five Italian serie A seasons with Genoa, may be over due to a nagging knee injury, doctors said on Tuesday.

The burly Czech, known as "Bomber" for his powerful headers, was attempting a comeback in the Czech first division with Viktoria Zizkov after failing to play while on loan with Portugal's Sporting Lisbon last season.
But after performing a routine physical on the 31-year-old striker on Monday, doctors said his right knee was badly damaged and advised him to stop playing.
Team officials said Skuhravy left the training facility visibly upset but saying nothing.
"Everybody at Viktoria is sorry about this because with his form, he could have helped us. But the most important thing is that he has his health," said Viktoria Director Petr Nemec.
In 49 appearances Skuhravy scored 17 goals for the former Czechoslovakia and the Czech Republic.
Skuhravy's finest hour came during the 1990 World Cup in Italy, where he scored five goals before Czechoslovakia were knocked out 1-0 by West Germany in the quarter-finals.

On the strength of his performance, including a three-goal binge against Costa Rica, Skuhravy attracted bids from Bayern Munich, Anderlecht and Italian club Torino. He signed for Genoa for a transfer fee of 3.5 billion lire ($2.8 million), the highest ever for a Czech player at the time.
